# Purpose

`build_contrast_analysis()` chains three steps:

1. a **strategy** says which model to fit per protein, e.g. `strategy_lm()`
2. `build_model()` fits it to every protein and returns a `Model`
3. `Contrasts` computes the contrasts from the models; `ContrastsModerated` shrinks their variances with the empirical Bayes method

This article runs the steps by hand for the `lm` method. Use them to inspect the per-protein models, to change one step, or to add a new modelling backend. For analyses, use `build_contrast_analysis()`.

```{r data}
library(prolfqua)
sim <- sim_lfq_data_protein_config(Nprot = 100, seed = 1234)
lfq <- LFQData$new(sim$data, sim$config)
contrasts <- c(AvsC = "group_A - group_Ctrl", BvsC = "group_B - group_Ctrl")
```

# The facade

```{r facade}
fa <- build_contrast_analysis(lfq, "~ group_", contrasts, method = "lm")
```

# The same, step by step

The `lm` method weights each protein intensity by its number of peptides, the column `lfq$nr_children_col()`.

```{r steps}
strat <- strategy_lm(paste(lfq$response(), "~ group_"), weights = lfq$nr_children_col())
mod <- build_model(lfq, strat)
contr <- Contrasts$new(mod, contrasts, model_name = "lm")
contr_mod <- ContrastsModerated$new(contr)
```

Both give the same result:

```{r same}
by_facade <- dplyr::arrange(fa$get_contrasts(), protein_Id, contrast)
by_hand <- dplyr::arrange(contr_mod$get_contrasts(), protein_Id, contrast)
all.equal(by_facade$diff, by_hand$diff)
all.equal(by_facade$p.value, by_hand$p.value)
```

The facade keeps the intermediate objects, so you can also take them from there: `fa$model` is the `Model`, `fa$contrast` the moderated contrasts.

# Inspecting the models

`mod$model_df` holds one row per protein with its fitted model and fit diagnostics.

```{r modelDf}
mod$model_df |>
  dplyr::select(protein_Id, has_model_fit, isSingular, nr_coef_not_NA, sigma, df.residual) |>
  head()
```

The analysis of variance per protein, and the distribution of its FDR:

```{r anova, fig.cap = "FDR of the per-protein analysis of variance."}
head(mod$get_anova())
mod$anova_histogram("FDR")$plot
```

The model coefficients:

```{r coefficients}
head(mod$get_coefficients())
```

# Without moderation

`Contrasts` alone gives the unmoderated contrasts, which the facades do not expose. Moderation stabilises the variances estimated from few observations:

```{r moderation}
data.frame(
  contrasts = c("Contrasts", "ContrastsModerated"),
  FDR_lt_0.1 = c(
    sum(contr$get_contrasts()$FDR < 0.1, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(contr_mod$get_contrasts()$FDR < 0.1, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)
```

# Changing one step

Replace the strategy to fit another model per protein, e.g. a robust linear model with `strategy_rlm()`; the other steps stay the same.

```{r rlm}
mod_rlm <- build_model(lfq, strategy_rlm(paste(lfq$response(), "~ group_")))
contr_rlm <- ContrastsModerated$new(Contrasts$new(mod_rlm, contrasts, model_name = "rlm"))
head(contr_rlm$get_contrasts()[, c("protein_Id", "contrast", "diff", "p.value", "FDR")])
```

# Adding a backend

A facade class wraps the steps of one method. `register_facade()` adds it to the registry, after which `build_contrast_analysis(method = ...)` finds it. `list_facades()` shows the registry:

```{r registry}
names(list_facades())
```
